references.text: God called Bezalel by name and filled him with His Spirit to perform artistic work for the tabernacle. This is the original appointment that Moses now conveys to the people.
The continuation of this text describes how God filled Bezalel with wisdom, understanding, and knowledge for all kinds of work.
Bezalel and Oholiab begin the work on the sanctuary, fulfilling the calling mentioned in this verse.
Bezalel son of Uri, son of Hur, of the tribe of Judah, made everything that the Lord had commanded Moses.
The genealogy of Bezalel through Caleb, showing his descent from Hur and Uri in the tribe of Judah.
Bezalel is mentioned as the craftsman who made the bronze altar, confirming his role in the construction of the tabernacle.
The same divine appointment of Bezalel is confirmed both by the giving of the law and by the command to begin the work.
A theological parallel in how God chooses leaders with specific gifts for various tasks.
Direct narrative continuation in the same chapter where Moses begins the work on the tabernacle.
